Subject: Visibility add-ons — looking to restructure & quantify savings

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. We like Redwood's visibility features, but the current packaging (retention + tracing + advanced dashboards) is a little hard to map to our internal chargeback model. Procurement asked me to see if we can: 

- collapse the three add-ons into a single "visibility" SKU for billing simplicity,
- get a clearer schedule for credits tied to committed storage/trace volume, and
- understand any technical scope changes (agents, retention TTLs, preview snapshots) that would affect our ops team.

Attached is our current SOW (Acme_SOW_v3.pdf) for reference. High level ask: can you propose 1) a compact pricing alternative, 2) a credit path if we commit to 12 months, and 3) any operational caveats we should include in the SOW?

Would you and your pricing/tech folks be available for a 30-minute call early next week?

Best,

Sam / Tessa — following up with the technical notes I promised. Key items to be aware of if Acme wants a single visibility SKU:

1) Retention tiers: we currently expose retention as a configurable TTL per dataset. For a single SKU we'd map three common tiers (30d / 90d / 365d) and default to 90d. If you want per-project overrides we can support it but that will complicate billing reconciliation.

2) Tracing ingestion: continuous-batching and KV cache optimizations mean peak ingestion cost is tied to span cardinality. For large bursty workloads we recommend a burst buffer (no code change) but need to document trace sampling expectations in the SOW.

3) Dashboards & snapshots: advanced dashboards use snapshotting; if you commit to 12 months we can retain snapshots for up to 180 days at no additional storage cost (subject to the agreed snapshot frequency).

4) Migration/agent footprint: if you adopt the unified SKU and choose the 365d tier, expect an initial data re-ingest (one-time job) for historical retention alignment — budget 2-3 engineer-days on your side.

I've attached a short technical worksheet that lists the migration tasks and estimated hours.

Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Attachment: technical-scope.xlsx (spreadsheet, 9 KB)

Hi Sam — thanks for the patience while we modeled options. Summary of commercial options (numbers illustrative — final spreadsheet attached to the HubSpot deal):

Option A — Metered (baseline)
- Keep retention, tracing, dashboards metered by usage. No upfront credits. Best if you want tight alignment to actual usage.

Option B — Slab (simplified SKU)
- Single monthly slab: 0-5TB, 5-25TB, 25TB+. Predictable billing, lower account complexity. 12-month commitment gets you a 12% credit applied monthly in arrears (reduces effective unit price).

Option C — Hybrid slab + credits (recommended)
- Slab tiers for billing simplicity + commitment credits for long-tail storage and snapshots. Example: commit to 15TB/month for 12 months -> 9% credit + one-time onboarding credit equal to 1 month of slab at your committed tier.

Operational caveats to include in the SOW:
- Data re-ingest estimate (Jordan listed 2-3 engineer-days),
- Trace sampling policy and burst buffer description,
- Snapshot frequency and retention window for dashboard snapshots.

Next steps: if you like Option C we will: 1) add a clause to the SOW for the onboarding credit, 2) produce an updated invoice schedule showing the monthly credit, and 3) mutually sign an amendment.

If that sounds good, Tessa will prepare the redlined SOW language and I can push the updated credit schedule to HubSpot (ACME-5421).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
